cases.question: What kind of matrix exchanges two rows?
cases.answer: A permutation matrix exchanges two rows [1][2]. Specifically, to exchange rows of a matrix, you can create a permutation matrix by exchanging the corresponding rows of the identity matrix [2].

cases.question: What matrix do you get by multiplying a square invertible matrix by its inverse?
cases.answer: You get the identity matrix. This is a key property of the inverse of a square matrix [2]. If a square matrix \( A \) has an inverse \( A^{-1} \), then \( A \cdot A^{-1} = I \) and \( A^{-1} \cdot A = I \), where \( I \) is the identity matrix [2].
